title: World's Best Lasagna
ingredients: 1.5 teaspoons salt, divided, or to taste
instructions: Cook sausage, ground beef, onion, and garlic in a Dutch oven over medium heat until well browned.

Stir in crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, and water. Season with sugar, 2 tablespoons parsley, basil, 1 teaspoon salt, Italian seasoning, fennel seeds, and pepper. Simmer, covered, for about 1 ½ hours, stirring occasionally.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook lasagna noodles in boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes. Drain noodles, and rinse with cold water.
In a mixing bowl, combine ricotta cheese with egg, remaining 2 tablespoons parsley, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

To assemble, spread 1 ½ cups of meat sauce in the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Arrange 6 noodles lengthwise over meat sauce, overlapping slightly. Spread with 1/2 of the ricotta cheese mixture. Top with 1/3 of the mozzarella cheese slices. Spoon 1 ½ cups meat sauce over mozzarella, and sprinkle with 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese.
Repeat layers, and top with remaining mozzarella and Parmesan cheese. Cover with foil: to prevent sticking, either spray foil with cooking spray or make sure the foil does not touch the cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for an additional 25 minutes.
Let the lasagna rest at room temperature for about 15 minutes before cutting; this helps it set and firm up.

most_helpful_positive_review.text: Excellent and Authentic recipe! A little more work and ingredients, but well worth it. Use FRESH basil for more flavor - I use about 1/2 - 2/3 cup fresh chopped basil. It cooks down and is sooo aromatic. The mix of sausage and beef is sublime, so no need for more salt. I always add a dash of nutmeg to the ricotta mixture (an old italian secret!). I usually make this a day ahead for the flavors and herbs to meld in the fridge then let it sit at room temperature for about 1 hour before baking. Have made for company too, and always get RAVES on it's authenticity. Great, winter comfort food and feeds a lot of people. Another tip for lasagna makers - no need to wash another pot to boil noodles. Soak raw, hard noodles in a large bowl of very hot tap water for 20-30 min. Noodles won't be cooked but soft, and can complete it's cooking in the oven. I learned this from a caterer - try it!

featured_tweaks.text:
This lasagna is great and the sauce itself is awesome too. My husband told me that this sauce is better that the one I usually make and that one was from his mother’s recipe. This recipe makes a little more sauce that you need so I use the leftover for some pasta or ravioli few days later. I followed some suggestions from the previous reviews and from making this recipe few times here are some things I changed. 
*Used 1lb each of beef and Italian sausage
*Used less salt (only about a teaspoon)
*Used only 1 tablespoon of sugar in the sauce
*Used wine instead of water
*Used fresh chopped basil instead of dry (about ½ cup)
*Used “ready to bake” lasagna noodles 
*Used fresh deli grade ricotta cheese not the processed stuff from the container
*Used freshly grated Parmesan cheese
This is a 5 start lasagna recipe that it better than the one you order in the restaurant!! I often add spinach (fresh spinach wilted with some butter) to the ricotta cheese and it tastes great. Remember to always use as much fresh ingredients as you can – you will taste the difference (fresh ricotta and Parmesan, add fresh parsley and basil etc) Enjoy! Also, make the sauce a day earlier to save time.

This is a good basic start, however, I felt it calls for too much salt and sugar.

I always add a pinch of sugar to neutralize the acid in tomato sauce, however, what I add is based on taste, and taste only. Some canned tomatoes and pastes have a sweeter taste than others, so I use taste as my only means for adding sugar.

This recipe was salt heavy for me - I've never added salt to ricotta and won't. Real ricotta has such a smooth, delicate flavor; I can't imagine what salt might do to it.

This is also very meaty. Though I prefer the blend of sausage/beef, I think it's a matter of personal preference. I also agree it needs more cheese, and we add different varities.

This is a good, basic recipe - add & modify as you wish, it is a solid foundation.

Made it for my husband’s birthday. Best lasagna either of us have EVER had - including at great Italian restaurants. I only used 1 can of tomato paste instead of two, an entire 15 oz. can of tomato sauce instead of two 6 oz. cans, 1 Tbsp. of sugar instead of two, and used 1 and 1/2 teaspoons dried oregano in place of the ‘Italian seasoning’. We love ricotta cheese, so I used 2 lbs. ricotta/ 2 eggs/ 1 tsp. nutmeg, adding 1/2 tsp. salt in total to the double batch of cheese. I didn’t use any other salt in the recipe. I also used one full pound of mozzarella that I shaved. I also used a full sized deeper metal ‘lasagna pan’ so the entire 1 lb. box of cooked noodles, all the cheeses and all the sauce made three nice layers of noodles with room on the top for oven baking without bubbling over the pan. The lasagna pan is bigger and deeper than a 9x13 inch pan, which really helps. I couldn’t believe how easily it cut and held it’s shape on the plates - even the first piece !! I assembled it the night before and baked the next evening. We toasted to John Chandler and his generous heart in sharing his fabulous recipe. My husband was thrilled with his birthday dinner last night and we can’t wait for leftovers tonight !!
The tomato paste is way too overpowering in this recipe.

Italian seasoning and tomato sauce are added ingredients. I use hot Italian sausage, which isn't very hot,but gives it more flavor than the sweet. Also, I cook my seasoning in a tablespoon of hot olive oil for about a minute, then I start the recipe from there. I believe cooking them releases their flavors rather than just adding them to the pot.

Never buy frozen lasagna again! This is easy to freeze after enjoying a couple freshly made portions. I use a silicone muffin pan and significantly overfill the cups (not pretty, but yummy). Two “muffins” = one single serving frozen lasagna.
This is an amazing lasagna recipe! I use the oven ready noodles so you don't have to boil them ahead of time. I also add red pepper flakes to the sauce. 10/10 best lasagna ever!

I've made this recipe about 15 times now. The last 3 times we've used our homemade tomato sauce that we canned in the fall and this time I made lasagna sheets from scratch. This is a crowd favorite for sure.

I made this a couple weeks ago. I used one pound of sage breakfast sausage, and one pound of hot, instead of the sweet Italian and beef blend (because that is what I had). Also I used Yo Mama’s low sodium marinara (again, because that is what I had), and no-salt added tomato paste and no salt tomato sauce, plus the herbs, and I used no-cook lasagna noodles. (Actually I have made this with standard noodles, without pre-boiling, and it comes out PERFECT, every time…growing up, my mom pre-boiled them, and her lasagna came out loosely goosey, and I prefer mine cooked, but al dente and the cut squares to be firm). I added no additional salt at all, because the parm and the mozzarella contribute a lot, and I have to be careful with salt. That said, we had our kids and grandkids over, and they slicked it right up and begged for more. It is really that good.

I made this for a family reunion and they absolutely loved it! I did double the ricotta and used 2 lbs of meat and 1 lb of sausage meat. I did 3 noodle layers instead of the suggested 2 layers. I boiled the noodles in a 9 x 13 glass dish to prevent the noodles from sticking. I boiled the water with olive oil. Then I laid the noodles in the pan. I added the boiling water to the pan and used a spatula to separate the noodles. I waited 30 minutes and the noodles were cooked perfectly. I did check on the noodles to make sure they weren't sticking to each other during that time. Everything came out great and was super delicious and flavorful! I can't wait to make it again! I would suggest to have some leftover sauce without the meat to coat the bottom of the pan and for the top layer. For the top layer it was just noodles and cheese (I usually place sauce on top of the noodles followed by cheese). It still was very good without the sauce on top, but maybe I will add the sauce the next time I make it. The sauce was not watery! I also didn't drain the fat from the meat because the directions never mentioned to do that, but I wonder if I should drain some of the fat next time as I thought the sauce was oily while it was simmering.
